To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

actin dynamics in dendrites and dendritic spines are regulated by synaptic activity, that these dynamic events are associated with changes of the actin‐based cytoskeleton in dendritic spine, and that these changes are important for the regulation of synaptic strength.
the cytoskeleton of dendritic spines is highly dynamic, that this dynamic behavior is regulated by synaptic transmission and that these changes occur in vivo.

the rapid, dynamic changes in actin observed in dendritic spiny neurons in vitro occur also in organized brain tissue, and that they are regulated by synaptic activity and by the postsynaptic receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the actin cytoskeletal system in the regulation of excitatory synaptic transmission.
the role of actin dynamics in dendrites and synapses of living neurons in culture.
the role of actin in synaptic plasticity, particularly the role of actins in dendritic spine morphological plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actin dynamics in spines are regulated by synaptic activity, and are involved in spine morphological changes, which are likely to be a mechanism of synaptic plasticity.

the actin cytoskeletal changes in dendritic spins are a form of regulated plastic changes in the morphology of excitatory synapses, which is a fundamental feature of synaptic transmission and plasticity.
actin dynamics are involved in the formation and maintenance of the spine head and that these dynamics are modulated by the activation of glutamate receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
actin dynamics are a form of regulated plastic change at excitatory synapse.
the actin cytoskeletal dynamics are involved in synaptic plasticity and that the actin dynamics are controlled by synaptic activity.
we have found that the spine is a dynamic structure and that the dynamics are regulated by synaptic transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
actin dynamics are a form of regulated plasticitiy at synapses.
there are two types of dendritic spine dynamics.

the actin cytoskeletal changes that are visible by microscopy in living neurons do correspond to changes in the shape of dendritic spines, and that the dynamics of these actin changes can be regulated by synaptic transmission.
